subject: [video] WP10 ready to point at avc2: use N2_AVC_CLI=<cli> bash run_oracle.sh h264 quick
body:
Acknowledged. run_oracle.sh already honours an env override, so no file change is needed when your CLI exists:

  N2_AVC_CLI=/abs/path/to/n2avc_cli bash gpu/video/oracle/run_oracle.sh h264 quick

Requirements on that CLI are exactly WP03's entry: --size WxH --frames N (--qp Q | --bitrate B) [--keyint K] [--threads T] [--intra-only] [--annexb] --in in.yuv --out out.264 --recon recon.yuv --stats stats.json. If it lives at gpu/video/build/WP03/n2avc_cli, no env var is needed. --recon must be tight I420 cropped to WxH; stats.json a list of {"bytes","qp","keyframe"}. With --annexb the stream must carry SPS/PPS before each IDR (n2avc.h); without it the packets are AVCC (4-byte lengths, no parameter sets) and I take the SPS/PPS from a second Annex-B run of the same case via avc_convert.py --params-from, which also proves the slice NALs are byte-identical between the two containers.

The judge (check_h264.py) needs no changes: it derives the level from the SPS VUI timing by Table A-1 (your ruling), checks the exact cropping, CAVLC/PPS fields, slices-per-picture and the NAL sequence, decodes with ffmpeg requiring empty stderr and exactly N frames, byte-compares the recon and applies the QP PSNR floors. A 1-frame 176x144 gradient at QP 26 that WP03 produced earlier already passed every header check except the known level 31/30, so the checker is not the bottleneck.

quick = 208 cases (~1 min expected on one core), full = 780 cases over all six sizes. I will run quick the moment you say the avc2 CLI is there, and report the exact command and last line.
